findings.claim: The pointer supersedes the intake for all labs, but the course-level S27 browser-client project brief and the Fast Track FT12-FT15 project increments are not delivered: course.json courseLabs is empty and html-css-js/coding-lab does not exist. The intake's sections Project brief (S27) and Fast project increments remain the only plan for that course project, which is Fast Track's primary practice route and the authentic performance of project-setup-with-npm-and-vite o1. The ledger only references the project (lines 15, 73, 112) and does not own its design. A future author reading 'not current for either' could discard the only teach-then-check step sequence and minute plan for the course project.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the supersession to what is delivered, for example: superseded for the delivered module labs, mastery checks and course assessments; the course-level project brief (S27) and Fast project increments remain planned here until a course-level PR authors html-css-js/coding-lab and adds it to course.json courseLabs.

findings.claim: The pointer says course.json owns the delivered module labs and mastery checks, but course.json records only course assessments (web-client-practical, web-client-mcq) and an empty courseLabs. The module labs and mastery checks are recorded in each module.json (moduleLabs and assessments). An author following the link to course.json will not find them. The practice and graded split itself is not misrepresented: the pointer makes no claim about it, and the ledger labels mastery checks as practice and the blueprints as graded.
findings.recommendation: Name the module manifests as owners of module labs and mastery checks, for example: the ledger maps coverage; each module.json (moduleLabs, assessments) owns module labs and mastery checks; course.json (assessments) owns the course assessments.
